requirements.requirement: On node1, root and opsadmin can schedule cron jobs, while all other users are denied.
requirements.summary: The final allowlist contains exactly root and opsadmin. Both users successfully created, listed, and removed crontabs before and after restart; the excluded user antrieb was denied. Temporary verification crontabs were removed.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The system remained CentOS 5.11 with kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 before and after execution. The implementation used the platform's installed cron access-control mechanism and introduced no software installation or upgrade.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct pre- and post-restart behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete and coherent. The only notable hygiene issue is one small abandoned reboot log in /tmp.
limitations: The lifecycle package-health collector invoked a yum operation unsupported on this legacy release, so package consistency was not independently established; however, the command timeline shows no package-management mutation.
Generic failed-service collection was unavailable because systemd is unsupported on CentOS 5; crond recovery was verified directly.

Denial was exercised behaviorally for antrieb rather than every possible account; the exact two-entry cron.allow file and captured platform documentation provide coherent evidence that all unlisted users are denied.

operational_hygiene.summary: Mutations creating opsadmin and /etc/cron.allow directly supported the task. Temporary crontabs and the temporary denial-check file were bounded evidence collection and were removed. The required restart protocol was complete: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered crond, configuration, accounts, and access behavior were all observed and independently corroborated by lifecycle boot identities. One unnecessary retained mutation was identified: cmd-97fa9cca43774135 created /tmp/benchmark-reboot.log, which remained after execution and was not shown to contribute evidence or be cleaned up.
